item.title: Road work slows traffic on I-10, local state roads this week
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers crossing Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should expect construction-related delays this week as maintenance crews tackle several state road projects. The Florida Department of Transportation says work is underway on Interstate 10 with resurfacing operations east of U.S. 231, along with activity on other state routes throughout the region.…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers crossing Escambia and Santa Rosa counties should expect construction-related delays this week as maintenance crews tackle several state road projects.

The Florida Department of Transportation says work is underway on Interstate 10 with resurfacing operations east of U.S. 231, along with activity on other state routes throughout the region. The agency typically posts weekly construction notices to alert commuters to potential slowdowns during peak travel times.

Motorists are advised to allow extra time for trips and watch for work zone signs. For real-time traffic updates and detailed project information, drivers can check the FDOT website or local traffic reports before heading out.

item.title: IMPACT 100 distributes record $1.313M to 13 nonprofits across Escambia, Santa Rosa counties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area announced Sunday that it has awarded $101,000 grants to 13 local nonprofit organizations, marking a record $1.313 million in total giving for the year. The grants were announced during the organization's Annual Meeting, reflecting the 23rd consecutive year that IMPACT 100 has distributed funds to nonprofits serving…
item.content:encoded:
IMPACT 100 Pensacola Bay Area announced Sunday that it has awarded $101,000 grants to 13 local nonprofit organizations, marking a record $1.313 million in total giving for the year. The grants were announced during the organization's Annual Meeting, reflecting the 23rd consecutive year that IMPACT 100 has distributed funds to nonprofits serving Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

The funding represents a significant boost for local charitable work across the region. IMPACT 100's grant program operates through a membership-driven model where donors pool contributions to support vetted nonprofit organizations working in education, health, social services, and community development.

The specific nonprofits receiving this year's awards were not immediately detailed in the announcement, though the $1.313 million total underscores growing community support for organized philanthropy in Northwest Florida.

item.title: Century Town Clerk Moore Earns State Professional Certification
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Carrie Moore, town clerk for the Town of Century, has earned her Florida Certified Professional Clerk (FCPC) designation, a credential conferred by the John Scott Dailey Florida Institute of Government at Florida State University in partnership with the Florida Association of City Clerks. The FCPC designation recognizes professional competency and…
item.content:encoded:
Carrie Moore, town clerk for the Town of Century, has earned her Florida Certified Professional Clerk (FCPC) designation, a credential conferred by the John Scott Dailey Florida Institute of Government at Florida State University in partnership with the Florida Association of City Clerks.

The FCPC designation recognizes professional competency and expertise in municipal clerk duties and administration. Moore's achievement reflects her commitment to professional development in local government service.

Century, located in north Escambia County, is one of the area's smaller municipalities. The certification underscores the importance local government places on ensuring clerks maintain current knowledge of state law, municipal operations, and best practices in public administration.

The driver is accused of blowing through multiple stop signs during the chase and holding a female passenger against her will. He's been charged with…
item.content:encoded:
A Cantonment resident faces felony charges following a high-speed pursuit in which he allegedly reached speeds of 115 mph while evading law enforcement, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The driver is accused of blowing through multiple stop signs during the chase and holding a female passenger against her will. He's been charged with felony fleeing and evasion as well as false imprisonment.

FHP did not immediately release additional details about where the pursuit took place or what prompted the initial traffic stop. The case remains under investigation.

item.content:encoded:
A Molino resident is facing serious felony charges following an alleged home invasion and violent assault, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Kent Gregory Harrell, 40, was arrested and charged with felony burglary with assault or battery and felony battery by strangulation. According to an arrest report, Harrell allegedly forced his way into a residence, where he choked and attempted to suffocate a woman with a pillow.

Details about the victim's condition or the circumstances leading to the arrest were not immediately released. The investigation remains ongoing.

item.title: Escambia County Clerk stalker ruled mentally fit for trial in firebombing case
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A man accused of stalking and threatening Escambia County Clerk of Court Pam Childers and setting fire to her neighbor's car has been found mentally competent to stand trial, according to court records. The suspect, who allegedly targeted Childers with threats and surveillance before the firebombing incident, was evaluated for his mental state as…
item.content:encoded:
A man accused of stalking and threatening Escambia County Clerk of Court Pam Childers and setting fire to her neighbor's car has been found mentally competent to stand trial, according to court records.

The suspect, who allegedly targeted Childers with threats and surveillance before the firebombing incident, was evaluated for his mental state as part of the criminal proceedings. The competency ruling clears the way for the case to move forward in Escambia County courts.

According to the criminal court docket, the defendant is now able to proceed to trial on charges related to the arson and the alleged stalking and threatening behavior directed at the clerk. The case represents a significant security concern for a county official, as the defendant's alleged actions appear to have targeted not only Childers but also resulted in property damage to a neighbor's vehicle.

item.title: Sunny fall weather to hold through week as high pressure builds
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola-area residents can expect an extended stretch of classic autumn conditions over the next several days, according to local weather reporting. Dry high pressure is settling over the region, bringing plenty of sunshine, comfortable afternoon temperatures, and crisp overnight lows typical of late October. The pattern looks set to continue…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola-area residents can expect an extended stretch of classic autumn conditions over the next several days, according to local weather reporting. Dry high pressure is settling over the region, bringing plenty of sunshine, comfortable afternoon temperatures, and crisp overnight lows typical of late October.

The pattern looks set to continue through the week, with a slight warming trend expected to develop as the week progresses. The combination of stable high pressure and dry air should keep rain chances minimal and skies mostly clear for outdoor activities and fall events across Escambia County and the surrounding area.

item.title: Escambia County Consolidates Storm Recovery Services to Single MARC Location
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County is consolidating its post-hurricane assistance operations into one site, effective immediately. The Multi-Agency Resource Center (MARC) previously operating at the Salvation Army Building on North Q Street has closed, with all services moving to the Bayview Senior Center at 2000 E. Lloyd Street in Pensacola. The consolidation…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is consolidating its post-hurricane assistance operations into one site, effective immediately. The Multi-Agency Resource Center (MARC) previously operating at the Salvation Army Building on North Q Street has closed, with all services moving to the Bayview Senior Center at 2000 E. Lloyd Street in Pensacola.

The consolidation streamlines county recovery efforts following recent storm damage. Residents seeking assistance with emergency aid, housing support, or other disaster-related services should now visit the Bayview Senior Center location.

County officials have not yet announced an end date for MARC operations at the consolidated site. Residents with questions about available services or eligibility can contact Escambia County Emergency Management for more information.

item.title: Free Diapers, Baby Food Distribution Set for Milton Wednesday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: State Representative Michelle Salzman is partnering with The Cutting Board and community organizers to distribute free diapers and baby food to Santa Rosa County families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. at The Cutting Board, 8855 FL-87 in Milton. Farm Share will supply an…
item.content:encoded:
State Representative Michelle Salzman is partnering with The Cutting Board and community organizers to distribute free diapers and baby food to Santa Rosa County families still recovering from Hurricane Isaias. The event is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28, from 4 to 6 p.m. at The Cutting Board, 8855 FL-87 in Milton.

Farm Share will supply an estimated 1,500 diapers in sizes 1, 3, and 5, plus 10 pallets of Beech-Nut baby food pouches. According to the press release, the distribution aims to help families access everyday necessities during the ongoing storm recovery period. "One of the things I love most about our community is how people come together when times get tough," Salzman said in a statement. "We want to be part of that kindness by helping local families with diapers and baby food and reminding them that they haven't been forgotten."

The Cutting Board owner Nan Foster emphasized that diapers and baby food are essential supplies during crisis recovery. "When a storm impacts our community, families with little ones face challenges that many people may not immediately think about," Foster said. Federal and state constituent services representatives will be on-site to connect families with additional resources. The event is open to the public, and free treats will be provided while supplies last.

item.title: Three Dead in Fiery Crash at Cervantes and M Street

The crash occurred when a vehicle traveling eastbound on Cervantes Street struck a barrier at M Street and became engulfed in flames. Multiple occupants were in the vehicle at the time of…
item.content:encoded:
At least three people were killed in a fiery vehicle crash overnight in Pensacola at the intersection of Cervantes and M Street, according to Pensacola Police.

The crash occurred when a vehicle traveling eastbound on Cervantes Street struck a barrier at M Street and became engulfed in flames. Multiple occupants were in the vehicle at the time of impact.

Pensacola Police responded to the scene. No additional details about the victims, the cause of the crash, or ongoing investigation have been released at this time.

item.title: Sunny Skies, Upper 70s Expected Through Early Week in Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A sprawling high pressure system is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, bringing classic fall weather that locals have been waiting for. Expect mostly sunny skies and dry conditions through Monday, with afternoon highs climbing to the mid-to-upper 70s—ideal for outdoor activities and weekend plans. Nights will turn crisp as…
item.content:encoded:
A sprawling high pressure system is settling over the North Escambia area this weekend, bringing classic fall weather that locals have been waiting for. Expect mostly sunny skies and dry conditions through Monday, with afternoon highs climbing to the mid-to-upper 70s—ideal for outdoor activities and weekend plans.

Nights will turn crisp as temperatures drop, typical for late October in Northwest Florida. The ridge of high pressure anchoring overhead should keep rain chances essentially zero through the weekend and into early next week, making this an excellent stretch for anyone looking to get outside without worrying about unexpected showers.

If you're planning any outdoor events or yard work around Pensacola, this is your window. The pattern looks stable, so don't expect any weather surprises to disrupt your Saturday or Sunday.
